title: OR Logic Gate (IC 7432)
summary: An OR gate is a fundamental digital logic gate that implements logical disjunction (Y = A + B). The output is HIGH (1) if AT LEAST ONE of its inputs is HIGH (1).

working_principle: When either input A or input B (or both) receives +5V (Logic 1), the internal transistor collector voltage rises, driving the output pin to +5V (Logic 1). Output is 0V only when both inputs are 0V.
mnemonic_trick: OR is ANY! Output is 1 if ANY input is 1. Output is ZERO ONLY when ALL inputs are 0!
applications: Alarm Systems (Triggered by Motion Sensor OR Door Sensor)
Combining Interrupt Signal Lines in Microcontrollers
Control Logic for Parallel Data Paths
advantages: Allows multiple event triggers to activate a single line
disadvantages: Cannot invert signals without additional NOT gates
common_mistakes: Expecting output 0 when both inputs are 1 (That is XOR, OR outputs 1 when both inputs are 1!).
quick_notes: Pin 14 is VCC (+5V), Pin 7 is GND.

interview_questions.q: How can you make an OR gate using only NOR gates?
interview_questions.a: Connect a 2-input NOR gate (7402) followed by a NOR gate configured as a NOT inverter.
